utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Let the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-01-48-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: May it please the Court, Your Honour, my name is Karl Koenig. I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor, along with my learned colleague Ms. Jocelyn Bodson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Faruk Balijagic, lead counsel for the accused Sefer Halilovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Balijagic. Well, this is the Status Conference according to the Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and the purpose of this hearing is to ensure an expeditious preparation of the case for trial and allow the parties, especially the Defence, to raise any issues relating to the case, relating to the status of the case. It is the opinion of the Court, the Trial Chamber, to have this case get ready for trial at the -- at least at the end of June of this year, and in order to do so, I would like first to know how many witnesses is the Prosecution going to call, to have -- to rely on at the trial, and of those witnesses, how many will be called live and how many will be submitted in the form of 92 bis statements. So I would like to hear from the Prosecution, first the answers to these questions relating to the number of witnesses and especially whether the Prosecution also thinks that this case can be ready at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The answers are definite and easy as possible. I'll give them to you like that. Your Honour, the Prosecution, at this stage, has relevant witnesses 200. We wouldn't intend calling 200 witnesses. A sample of those would be suggested, but that would depend on the talks that we had with the Defence. As His Honour may or may not know, there has been substantial cooperation between the Prosecution and the Defence. We have spent a very long time in the last month or two interviewing the accused, and there seems to be a lot of common ground. What hasn't been done as yet is we haven't sat down and spoken about the agreed facts between us, and that would certainly reduce the number of witnesses. The likelihood of there being agreed facts in this case is particularly high. It would seem that the area of dispute is somewhat narrower than we envisaged at the outset. So to give His Honour the accurate rendition of the number of witnesses that we will require -- we would call now simply is dependent on what the Defence has to say. I can give His Honour an estimation. We would estimate about 30 witnesses per count. That would deal with crime scene witnesses; it would deal with experts; it would deal with military witnesses. Of those, we would also estimate that there would be a total of at least 15 to 20 of the witnesses we may be able to call by means of a statement without having them being as a live witness. Whether or not we would be able to be ready by the end of June depends on the further cooperation that we have with the accused. It is scheduled that we would be speaking to the accused again after receiving further documentation. We have received a lot of documentation from the accused already. Mr. Balijagic has kindly brought some further documentation for us today. So in that respect, there is some further investigation that we need to follow and check up on. As His Honour is aware, of course there are quite serious problems with translation, and we have a number of document collections which haven't even begun to be translated. Those would involve, of course, disclosure in terms of Rule 68, should there be any to the accused, and it may be that in fact the accused has invoked or will be invoking Rule 68(B), reciprocal disclosure, which would mean that we would have to then disclose the rest of that documentation. That would be a mammoth task. I hope that, to some extent, answers Your Honour's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is my understanding that the supporting materials of the indictment, which is provided by the Rule 66(A)(i), have been already handed over to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could perhaps just give His Honour a brief summary of the disclosure up to now, it may assist. The complete material has been made over to the Defence. Initially, the English version was made over two days after the first appearance. The remainder was done within the prescribed period by the Rules in a language that he is able to understand. There was a further document that had been requested by the Defence that has also been made over, and the documentation under Rule 68, the statement side, most of that has already been made over to the Defence. The documentation side hopefully will be made over within the next two weeks and then, of course, there is the ongoing disclosure under Rule 68 and further statements that have been taken that will be made over hopefully within the next month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So there's no -- it's more a translation problem in relation to those materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: There's a translation problem in relation to that and the other documentation that most of us haven't even been through yet. It's just arrived in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's begin with some specific and technical problems. When do you think you can disclose the witness statements to the Defence, according to the Rule 66(A)(i)[sic]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are hoping to do the remainder of the statements that we have under 66(i)[sic] within the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the Rule 92 bis witness statements, together with its applications?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I've said, we are looking at about 20 witnesses per count. In that respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but what do you mean by "per count"? We have only one count in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Sorry. I beg your pardon. Per incident. There are two incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. May I repeat: 20 to 30?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: About that per incident, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll have about 40 to 60 witnesses, according to what you are saying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then -- so when is it possible for you to apply to file and application for the 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be a pure estimation, but I'd imagine, to be able to get those number of witnesses seen and done, two to three months. Your Honour, I just conferred with my chief investigator, and he suggests that I'm perhaps a little bit optimistic in respect of two to three months. He suggests more like four to five months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the pre-trial brief for the Prosecution? Do you think you can file the pre-trial brief together with the 92 bis application at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, that is possible, provided -- or depending on the degree of the documentation and the assistance we get from the accused. During the course of the interview with the accused, there's a number of relevant documents and a lot of relevant evidence that we have needed to check and still needs to be checked, and that certainly may alter the Prosecution's stance in respect of the Prosecution itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, it is the opinion of the Court to make the case Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be ready for trial as soon as possible, and you are saying that you need at least some time of four months from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: At least, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be possible to make it in three months?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: I really don't think so, Your Honour. We have -- the particular team that deals with incidents is a very small team, and we have quite limited resources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That means that you think you can complete your filing of the pre-trial brief at the end of May -- at the end of April? That will be about four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: That would be a push, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, thank you, Mr. Koenig.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid I might miss some part of your sentence. What happens to the translation? Tell me about some circumstances about translation of these witness statements. Isn't there any problem to file it before the end of April, considering the translation problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not the translation of the witness statements that's the problem. It's the translation of the documentation that's a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: And there's thousands of documents, and we're certainly not on top of the priority list. We're well down the priority list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: And my learned colleague makes the point as well that we then have to look through the documentation once we've got a translation to decide whether it's particularly relevant for us or in terms of Rule 68. And when you're looking at thousands and thousands of documents, that's going to take quite a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Balijagic, I'd like to hear from you. How long do you think you need to prepare the Defence in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Your Honour, unfortunately, I will not be able to be as precise as my learned friend opposite in view of the specific nature of the indictment. Allow me to use a Latin saying which is often referred to in our courts: "Diogenes aliquando lucernam genstas ambulabat rogatus quid ageret respondit hominem quero." "Diogenes once, at noon, was walking around the square with a light in his hand, and asked what he was doing, he said, `I'm looking for a man.'" . My client, Sefer Halilovic, ever since the 9th of September, 1993, the date of the offence, the crimes, sought to have the criminals punished. However, he has not managed at all to this day, except by achieving full cooperation with the Prosecution since the indictment was issued, and we hope through this cooperation that we will assist the Court in passing a fair judgement. Indeed, we have been working for about two and a half months with the Office of the Prosecutor, working hard, up to ten hours a day, and we have collected quite a number of documents which throw a somewhat different light on this case. Originally, we had prepared some 350 statements under oath and 50 witnesses who would be heard in court, and a new file of documents, too, which were not accessible either to the Prosecution or the Court so far, because as you know, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the government has changed. My client, Sefer Halilovic, who was indicted for the crime of genocide, and it was instead of him that his brother was punished by that nationalist regime which has now changed. And we are now continuing cooperation in Sarajevo with the Prosecution with the disclosure of new documents, and we will need quite a bit of time because since the indictment was issued, we have not had time to prepare a good quality defence. So that it is the opinion of the Defence that we will need at least a year to prepare properly. But I also hope that the Prosecution, who are, I'm sure, concerned about the rule of law, will change certain provisions in the indictment. And it is indeed, as I said, difficult for me to give you a precise answer until our next Status Conference, because everything depends on our future cooperation, which we are continuing in Sarajevo as of this month. I hope you will be able to appreciate the specifics of the situation and show a spirit of tolerance for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Balijagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said that a year is needed, but having heard from the Prosecution that they are ready to file their pre-trial brief until the end of April, more specifically, Mr. Balijagic, how long do you think you need to file your pre-trial brief of the Defence after having received the pre-trial brief of the -- trial brief from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we're under pressure of time, after receiving the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution, we would need another four months for our brief. But I wish to underline once again that I am firmly convinced, as being a lawyer with 20 years of experience behind me, I'm quite confident that the Prosecution, having reviewed all the documents, will amended the indictment and, in doing so, that we will be assisting the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, let's make it as a kind of prospective timetable. Is it okay with you that we will -- provided that the Prosecution will file their pre-trial brief at the end of April, can you file your pre-trial brief at the end of July, which means about some 31st of July, Wednesday or something like that. Just a tentative one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we'll have to, Your Honour, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Will there be -- I'm sorry. Will there be any application for protective measures regarding the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Not at this stage, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just raise one point more? My learned colleague, who will be the Senior Trial Attorney conducting the matter, does want to stress that April is provided everything is well and there are no further problems in respect of translation and receipt of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I see that we have to have another Status Conference before that date, so we can -- we have another opportunity to deal with that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All right. Are there any issues the parties wish to raise at this moment? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: None from our side, Your Honour, just to say that the cooperation has been good and is continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence also has no further matters to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, let's make it clear that the -- temporarily but largely as a principle that the parties will adhere to, but the Prosecution will file its pre-trial brief on -- what's the date? 30th is the holiday, national holiday. So about 29th. Yes, Monday, 29th of April. And together with this, all the disclosure of witness statements, including the 92 bis statements, to the Defence. And then the Defence will respond to that with a pre-trial brief of its own at the end of July. That is also Monday, the 31st of July. No. I'm sorry. I'm mistaken. 31st, Wednesday, of July. Yes. Then we'll have the next Status Conference. Do you have any opinion about that, Mr. Koenig?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOENIG
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It really depends up to the Court's pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the Defence, Mr. Balijagic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BALIJAGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence also has no objection. We're in your hands, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Today is Tuesday. We'll have the hearing on Tuesday. Let's make it a principle. About two weeks before the due date of the Prosecution's pre-trial brief. So that will be about 16th of April, Tuesday, and the specific time and courtroom will be -- I will let you know afterwards, after having checked the courtroom circumstances. According to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Pre-Trial Judge is-may be assisted by the Senior Legal Officer, one of the senior legal officers assigned to the Chamber, in performing his duties. So in this regard, I'd like to have Ms. Yvonne Featherstone assist me in the way of meeting and communicating with the parties on a regular basis, such as once a month, between the hearing dates, to discuss and consult the matters relating to the status of the case. So I want the parties to meet with Ms. Featherstone after this hearing, not leaving the courtroom, about fixing a date for the next appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If there is not anything else for the parties to raise at this moment, the Court is adjourned, and the next Status Conference will be held Tuesday, 16th of April.
